messages:
Sam (Hiring): Mia accepted the offer today, start date June 1. She's currently in the UK and needs H-1B consular stamping. Wants to start remotely from London until stamping is done. Can we onboard her as an employee outside the US?
Elena (People Ops): Short answer: not directly. Redwood doesn't have a local entity in UK for US hires. Options: delay US payroll until stamping and entry, hire via EOR in UK for interim, or engage as a contractor (legal/tax risk). Need guidance from immigration + payroll.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Immigration side: H-1B beneficiaries generally need consular visa to enter if they're abroad; remote work outside US is allowed but changes tax/residency and may impact H-1B status start date. If she works abroad before entry, the H-1B start date may still be the petition start but she won't be in H-1B until admitted. Recommend clarifying with tax and global mobility.
Jorge (Payroll): Payroll note: we can't put someone on US payroll while they are physically working in the UK without entity and local tax withholding. We can do retro-pay if she later enters, but benefits and US-employee programs (401k, US health plans) can't be applied while on EOR or contractor. EOR costs ~15-20% of salary.
Zoe (Global Mobility): EOR available as short-term solution. We typically use an EOR partner for up to 6 months while hiring completes. Need signed local paperwork, UK payroll set-up, pension auto-enrolment checks. That adds 2-3 business days to start once candidate signs.
Mia (Candidate): I prefer to start earlier remotely if possible. Concerned about losing momentum. I'm happy to do contractor via local invoice if that helps, but want clarity on benefits and taxes.
Elena (People Ops): If contractor, benefits won't apply and we need clear contractor agreement + independent contractor screening. People Ops prefers EOR for continuity of benefits-like perks (limited) and company headcount tracking.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Also note: if she bills as contractor while H-1B approved, that could be considered unauthorized employment in certain circumstances. We need to avoid overlapping status issues. Best to route through EOR or delay US employment until stamping/entry.
Jorge (Payroll): Action items: 1) confirm EOR quote and timeline (Zoe). 2) Candidate decision: EOR vs wait. 3) If EOR, collect UK ID docs and completed local forms. 4) If waiting, confirm deferred start and payroll onboarding checklist.
Zoe (Global Mobility): I'll get EOR pricing and turnaround by EOD and post here.
hr-bot: Reminder: add "visa-stamp-remote-onboard" tag to candidate file and set follow-up for 3 business days.
Sam (Hiring): Thanks all  priority is to keep Mia engaged. Mia, we can do weekly check-ins and access to docs/repos. Please tell us preference ASAP so we can finalize.
Mia (Candidate): Thanks everyone. Please send EOR cost and I'll decide by tomorrow. Appreciate the flexibility.
Elena (People Ops): Noted. We'll pause US benefits enrollment until payroll status confirmed. If EOR chosen, we'll map entitlements and prorate where applicable.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): I'll draft a short advisory we can share with Mia explaining implications for H-1B status and timing.
